# Sirach 11 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 11 (34 verses)
**Total Disagreements:** 18

---

## Disagreement 1 — Verse 2

**Issue:** Rendering of the paired terms for "appearance/form"
- EMET: "Do not praise a man for his appearance, and do not loathe a man for his outward form"
- LOGOS: "Do not praise a man for his beauty, nor despise a man for his appearance"
- PNEUMA: "Never judge by appearances — beauty is no basis for praise, nor ugliness for contempt"
- SOPHIA: "Do not praise a man for his appearance, nor despise anyone on account of how he looks"

**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET's structure but drops the parallel noun "form." LOGOS "beauty" interprets Greek morphē more specifically. PNEUMA expands freely. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 2 — Verse 4

**Issue:** "Clothing" (στολή) and tone of warning
- EMET: "Do not boast about the clothing you wear"
- LOGOS: "Do not boast about your fine clothing"
- PNEUMA: "Don't brag about your fine wardrobe"
- SOPHIA: "Do not boast about the clothes you wear"

**Resolution:** LOGOS and PNEUMA add "fine" as an interpretive gloss. EMET/SOPHIA more literal. Minor difference; SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 3 — Verse 4b

**Issue:** "Works hidden from men"
- EMET: "his deeds among men are hidden"
- LOGOS: "his works are concealed from men"
- PNEUMA: "much of what he does among people stays hidden"
- SOPHIA: "his works among people remain hidden"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA adds "much of" weakening the absolute statement. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS structure. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 4 — Verse 10

**Issue:** Structure of triple conditional
- EMET: "if you multiply your affairs, you will not go unpunished; and if you pursue, you will not overtake"
- LOGOS: "if you multiply activities, you will not go unpunished; if you pursue, you will not overtake"
- PNEUMA: "If you pile up commitments, you'll pay for it. If you chase after everything, you'll catch nothing"
- SOPHIA: "if you multiply activities, you will not go unpunished. If you pursue, you will not overtake"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA's "you'll pay for it" loses the unpunished/punished legal connotation. EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA essentially agree. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 5 — Verse 12

**Issue:** Extent of description of the sluggard
- EMET: "who is sluggish and lacks strength, who falls short in prosperity"
- LOGOS: "who is slow, who needs assistance, who lacks ability"
- PNEUMA: "Others are slow and weak, in need of help"
- SOPHIA: "who is sluggish and needs help, who lacks strength and falls short"

**Resolution:** Three somewhat different expansions of the Greek. SOPHIA harmonizes EMET and LOGOS. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 6 — Verse 14

**Issue:** List of paired opposites — inclusion of "life and death"
- All agents agree on the list: good/evil, life/death, poverty/wealth
- Difference only in "riches" vs. "wealth"
- EMET/PNEUMA/SOPHIA: "wealth"; LOGOS: "riches"

**Resolution:** Minor. "Wealth" preferred for contemporary register. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 7 — Verse 15

**Issue:** "Everlasting success" vs. "enduring success"
- EMET: "his favor brings success everlasting"
- LOGOS: "his favor leads to everlasting success"
- PNEUMA: "his favor flourishes forever"
- SOPHIA: "his favor leads to enduring success"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA shifts metaphor ("flourishes"). SOPHIA uses "enduring" as slightly less absolute than "everlasting" while preserving the sense. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 8 — Verse 19

**Issue:** Tone of the rich fool's speech
- EMET: "I have found rest, and now I will eat of my goods"
- LOGOS: "I have found rest, and now I will enjoy my goods"
- PNEUMA: "I can finally rest — now I'll enjoy what I've saved"
- SOPHIA: "I have found rest, and now I will enjoy my goods"

**Resolution:** EMET "eat of" is more literal (Greek φάγομαι). LOGOS/SOPHIA "enjoy" is more idiomatic. PNEUMA's "what I've saved" is an addition. LOGOS/SOPHIA preferred for readability; the eating metaphor is not lost in context. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 9 — Verse 21

**Issue:** "Suddenly and swiftly" vs. "suddenly"
- EMET: "to enrich a poor man suddenly and swiftly"
- LOGOS: "to make a poor man suddenly rich"
- PNEUMA: "he can make a poor person rich in an instant"
- SOPHIA: "to make a poor person suddenly rich"

**Resolution:** EMET doubles up on adverbs; LOGOS/PNEUMA/SOPHIA use one. Greek ἐν ριπῇ supports a single swift moment. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 10 — Verse 22

**Issue:** "Causes his blessing to flourish" vs. "makes his blessing flourish"
- EMET: "he causes his blessing to flourish"
- LOGOS: "he makes his blessing flourish"
- PNEUMA: "his blessing blooms"
- SOPHIA: "he makes his blessing flourish"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA drops the subject. Minor variation. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 11 — Verse 25

**Issue:** Active/passive construction
- EMET: "evil things are forgotten … good things are not remembered"
- LOGOS: "adversity is forgotten … prosperity is not remembered"
- PNEUMA: "hard times are forgotten … good times fade from memory"
- SOPHIA: "evil is forgotten … good things are not remembered"

**Resolution:** LOGOS "adversity/prosperity" reads more abstractly. PNEUMA "fade from memory" is more vivid. SOPHIA harmonizes toward literal. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 12 — Verse 27

**Issue:** "At the end of a man" — how to render
- EMET: "at the end of a man his deeds will be revealed"
- LOGOS: "at the end, a man's deeds are revealed"
- PNEUMA: "it is what a person does at the end that tells the real story"
- SOPHIA: "at the end, a person's deeds are revealed"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA expands significantly. EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA close. "person" preferred for inclusivity. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 13 — Verse 28

**Issue:** Famous maxim "do not call anyone blessed before death"
- EMET: "Before death, do not call anyone blessed; and a man will be known by his end, how his children are"
- LOGOS: "Do not call anyone blessed before his death; a man will be recognized by his end, and by his children"
- PNEUMA: "Don't declare anyone blessed before their death — only at the end will a person's true character be known, through both their deeds and their children"
- SOPHIA: "Do not call anyone blessed before his death — a man will be known by his end, and by his children"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA adds "their deeds" not in the Greek. EMET "how his children are" awkward. LOGOS/SOPHIA preferred. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 14 — Verse 29

**Issue:** "Snares of the deceitful" vs. "wiles of the crafty"
- EMET: "many are the snares of the deceitful"
- LOGOS: "many are the wiles of the crafty"
- PNEUMA: "crafty people set all kinds of traps"
- SOPHIA: "the crafty set many a snare"

**Resolution:** Both snares/wiles and deceitful/crafty are valid. SOPHIA blends both. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 15 — Verse 30

**Issue:** "Decoy partridge" imagery
- EMET: "Like a decoy partridge in a cage"
- LOGOS: "Like a caged partridge used as a lure"
- PNEUMA: "A proud person is like a decoy bird in a cage"
- SOPHIA: "Like a caged decoy partridge"

**Resolution:** All capture the sense. "Decoy partridge" is the most specific to the Greek κίχλη/πέρδιξ tradition. SOPHIA condenses. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 16 — Verse 31

**Issue:** "Turning good into evil" — active vs. passive subject
- EMET: "he lies in wait, turning good into evil"
- LOGOS: "he turns good things into evil"
- PNEUMA: "They twist what is good into something bad"
- SOPHIA: "He turns good into evil"

**Resolution:** EMET includes "lies in wait" from v.32 context. SOPHIA follows LOGOS brevity. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 17 — Verse 32

**Issue:** "A sinner lies in wait for blood" — metaphor clarity
- EMET: "a sinful man lies in wait for blood"
- LOGOS: "a sinner lies in ambush for blood"
- PNEUMA: "a sinner is always lying in wait for someone's blood"
- SOPHIA: "a sinner lies in wait for blood"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA adds "always" and "someone's." SOPHIA stays literal. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 18 — Verse 34

**Issue:** Consequence of admitting a stranger
- EMET: "he will create trouble for you, and will estrange you from your own household"
- LOGOS: "he will upset you with turmoil, and will alienate you from your own family"
- PNEUMA: "they'll fill it with chaos, and you'll find yourself a stranger to your own family"
- SOPHIA: "he will throw you into turmoil, and estrange you from your own household"

**Resolution:** All capture the sense. SOPHIA blends EMET's "household" with LOGOS' "turmoil." SOPHIA adopted.
